# Events, webhooks and jobs

React to changes, deliver them to other systems, and run work in the background.

- [Events](../reference/events.md#declaring-events): A resource declares named events, such as an order that was created or a status that changed.
- [Change capture](../reference/events.md#how-changes-are-captured): Every change is captured in the database, in the same transaction, whoever made it.
- [Webhooks](../reference/webhooks.md#subscription): Events are sent to a URL, an API function or your own code, filtered by event, condition and tenant.
- [Signed webhooks](../reference/webhooks.md#what-a-receiver-gets): Deliveries are signed under the Standard Webhooks spec.
- [Delivery retries](../reference/webhooks.md#delivery-and-retries): Failed deliveries are retried for about three days.
- [Webhooks in the admin app](../reference/webhooks.md#subscriptions-in-the-admin-app): Users create subscriptions, send test events and resend failures in the app.
- [Background jobs](../reference/jobs.md#enqueueing): Jobs are kept in the app's own Postgres and can be queued in the same transaction as a write, also from SQL.
- [Retries](../reference/jobs.md#failures): Failed jobs are retried with growing waits, and duplicates can be prevented with a key.
- [Ordered groups](../reference/jobs.md#ordered-groups): Jobs in one group run one at a time, in order.
- [Recurring jobs](../reference/jobs.md#recurring-jobs): Jobs run on a cron schedule in a chosen time zone.
- [Failed jobs page](../reference/jobs.md#failed-jobs-page): Admins see jobs that failed for good and retry or delete them.
- [Jobs on hosts that sleep](../reference/jobs.md#hosts-that-sleep): A host that stops idle apps can wake them when a job is due.
